rounds.text: Crest Ventures Ltd is visibly discounted by the market, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.78x against a book value of ₹ 459 per share while the stock sits at ₹ 357 [E2]. This asset-backed discount is further supported by an intrinsic valuation via discounted cash flow analysis which places value at ₹ 482 per share, offering a margin of safety of 25.9% [E39, E40]. Long-term operating metrics demonstrate structural substance, highlighted by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 24% and a stellar 5-year compounded profit growth of 73% [E15, E19]. Financial health remains robust with conservative financing reflected by a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.22x and comfortable short-term liquidity shown by a current ratio of 3.55x as of March 2026 [E33, E34]. Furthermore, management confidence is underscored by promoters increasing their stake to 69.84% by September 2026 from 69.11% in December 2023 [E36], while technical momentum confirms strength with the price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E44]. conceded: [E16], [E17], [E20], [E21].

Crest Ventures Ltd carries significant fundamental deterioration and valuation risks that are masked by surface-level asset metrics. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and 3 years has cratered to -34% and -37% respectively [E16, E17], while compounded profit growth over the same periods stands at -49% and -51% [E20, E21], culminating in a severe net profit drop of -58% year-over-year [E62]. Profitability is severely depressed, evidenced by a trailing median return on equity of just 4% [E29] and a 3-year average ROE of 5.68% [E54], which badly trails the broader sector benchmark of 5.13% [E9] and leaves capital efficiency exceptionally weak. Furthermore, structural operational bloat is evident as working capital days have dramatically ballooned from 860 days to an alarming 1,305 days [E56]. Valuation multiples are also stretched relative to peers, with a trailing P/E of 30.4x versus a sector benchmark of 19.16x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 15.92x against a sector benchmark of 13.14x [E11]. Compounding these concerns, foreign institutional investors have aggressively dumped their holdings, slashing their stake from 4.74% in December 2023 to 1.61% by September 2026 [E37]. Finally, the equity suffers from extreme historical risk characteristics, highlighted by a staggering worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -94.7% [E47] and high annualised volatility of 56.2% [E48]. Conceded: the company trades at a discount to book value with a P/B of 0.78x [E2], boasts a solid current ratio of 3.55x [E34], and features an expanding promoter stake now standing at 69.84% [E36].

The bear’s focus on recent growth deceleration ignores the company’s proven ability to scale, as evidenced by a 24% compounded sales growth and 73% compounded profit growth over the last five years [E15, E19]. While the bear highlights recent volatility, the stock’s 10-year compounded share price growth of 15% demonstrates long-term resilience [E22]. The criticism of valuation multiples ignores the most critical metric for a company of this nature: the price-to-book ratio of 0.78x, which sits significantly below the sector benchmark of 1.25x [E7, E53]. Conceded: the bear is correct that working capital days have increased to 1,305 [E56] and that foreign institutional holdings have decreased [E37]. However, the bear fails to acknowledge that promoters have increased their stake to 69.84%, signaling strong internal confidence in the company’s recovery [E36]. Furthermore, the company maintains a robust financial foundation with a current ratio of 3.55x and conservative debt levels [E33, E34], providing the necessary stability to navigate cyclical downturns [E52]. Finally, the current market price offers a 25.9% margin of safety relative to the intrinsic value derived from a discounted cash flow analysis [E40, E59].

Conceded: five-year compounded sales growth is 24% and profit growth is 73% [E15, E19], and promoters hold 69.84% [E36]. However, pointing to a 0.78x price-to-book ratio [E7] ignores that this low valuation is justified by abysmal returns, with ROE sitting at 3.8% to 4% and a 3-year median ROE of just 6% [E13, E28, E29]. The bull's reliance on historical 10-year share price growth [E22] glosses over severe recent deterioration, evidenced by a 3-year sales contraction of -37%, a 3-year profit contraction of -51%, and a recent net profit drop of -58% year-on-year [E16, E20, E62]. Furthermore, citing a current ratio of 3.55x [E34] and conservative debt [E33] does not excuse crippling operational inefficiency, as working capital days have ballooned to an alarming 1,305 days [E56]. Finally, the claimed discounted cash flow margin of safety [E40] relies on growth assumptions that directly contradict the company's current trajectory of decelerating earnings and negative trailing twelve-month sales growth of -34% [E17, E63].
